column1: # deep32-wizard-hv.tsv: the Workstation VM guide's hypervisors, settings, steps and checks.
# Both wizards (deep32-wizard.sh and deep32-wizard.ps1) read this one file, so their screens, steps and checks
# cannot drift apart. Lines starting with # are comments; blank lines are ignored. Fields are separated by one TAB;
# "-" is an empty field. Text is ASCII. In text, `backticks` mark a command (shown whole, on a line of its own),
# " | " separates the numbered items of a step, and {name} is filled in by the wizard:
#   {kit} {copy} {copyname} {gethv}                 deep32-get's VM folder and its installer copy
#   {disc2} {disc2name} {dl} {sep} {vdi}             disc 2, the download folder, the path separator, the VDI copy
#   {hvname} {net} {netlabel} {nodeimage} {ts-stall} the choices made on the earlier screens, and text ts-stall
# The wizard never creates, changes, starts or stops a VM: every command here is for the person to run.
# The official pages every hypervisor value rests on are listed at the end of this file.
# hv     ID  NAME  BOOT-TESTED(yes|no)  THIS-PC(found|always|windows|unix|never)  LOCAL-CHECK  TOOLS  NETWORKS
# field  HV  WHERE(here|other|bridged|nat|*)  KEY  LABEL  DEFAULT  PATTERN  ERROR  HELP
# step   HV  WHERE  NET(bridged|nat|*)  OS(unix|windows|*)  ID  CHECK  TITLE  PLACE  BODY  LOOK-FOR
#        CHECK: image, copy, vmdk, vdi, vm:create, vm:after (add +look to also ask for LOOK-FOR), join, confirm
# rule   HV(*|id)  PHASE  FACT  OP(eq|ne|ge|in|has)  VALUE  CODE (a row of deep32-wizard-errors.tsv)
# fix    HV  CODE  STEPS (replaces the error table's steps for this hypervisor)

column3: Bridged: the Workstation gets an address on your LAN from the router's DHCP, like any other machine there. Tailscale usually connects directly between machines on the same LAN, which is the fastest path. Recommended.
NAT: also works; the Workstation only needs outbound internet. Tailscale may relay through its DERP servers when it cannot connect directly, which is slower for Ask, the Library and the Forge.
Host-only, internal and private networks do not work: the Workstation has no internet there, so its Tailscale sign-in cannot finish.
{hvname} connects VMs to your LAN through a bridge, so the Workstation is bridged.
deep32-get's recipe puts the VM on libvirt's default network, which is NAT. For a host bridge, check your hypervisor's manual.
the node's bridge, vmbr0 unless you name another next
a port group on a virtual switch that reaches your LAN
Bridged networking, to a host network adapter you name next
a wired network with DHCP and internet

Deep32 machines talk over your tailnet, so the Workstation, the Forge and the agent PC can be in different places. At home on one LAN the connections are direct. Across sites they still work; the speed depends on whether Tailscale gets a direct path or relays.
The Workstation signs in to Tailscale at its first boot. It shows the sign-in address on its console.

Publication (d32-publish publish --accept-ct) gives the gateway an HTTPS name on your tailnet. That name appears in public certificate-transparency logs. Only the name: the gateway is still reachable only inside your tailnet.
Tailscale access rules (ACLs) must let the agent PC and the Forge reach the Workstation. If your tailnet has custom rules, allow them; the default policy allows everything.
The Workstation checks DNSSEC through the DNS server DHCP gives it. A few routers' DNS breaks that and the sign-in stalls. Then give the VM's network another DNS server.
